statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains low because fresh Asian-market reporting is mixed and no sufficiently current independent source confirms persistent one-way NQ structure; oil near $107 and the 10-year yield near 5% keep Stress extreme.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The next evidence-heavy danger window is the 12:30 UTC Empire State release through the first full U.S. cash-session hour; higher Tail states remain conditional on observed directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks or failed retracements.
headline: Tail remains low while oil and near-5% yields keep cross-asset Stress extreme
body: Fresh Reuters reporting shows mixed Asian equities, Brent near $107 and the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield around the 5% threshold. Monday's semiconductor selloff remains a background vulnerability. No sufficiently current independent source verifies persistent one-way NQ price structure, so Tail stays below WATCH.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 UTC clock hours, Tail remained elevated through Monday's overnight and early U.S. session, peaking at 32%, then fell as substantial intraday mean reversion emerged. WATCH persisted around 16-17 UTC and briefly at 20 UTC; Tail stayed low from 21 UTC through 03 UTC.
outlookSummary: Current Tail remains low because fresh Asian risk is mixed and persistent one-way NQ structure is not independently verified. Conditional risk rises into the 12:30 UTC Empire State release and 13:30 UTC cash open, peaking at 24% WATCH only if price discovery becomes persistently directional with shallow or failed retracements.

forecast.analysis: Asia is mixed; Brent is near $107 and the 10-year yield near 5%. Live NQ path evidence is insufficient to confirm mean-reversion failure.
